bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Internal Revenue Service relating to "Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales".
bill.latestActionText: Message received in Senate: Returned to the Senate pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 212.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the rule titled Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales and issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) on December 30, 2024. The rule generally requires persons effectuating decentralized financial (DeFi) transactions to report certain information regarding digital asset sales to the IRS.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution would block a December 2024 IRS rule that requires brokers and platforms facilitating digital asset (cryptocurrency) sales to report transaction details and gross proceeds to the IRS. The rule was designed to improve tax compliance by ensuring the IRS receives information about cryptocurrency sales, similar to reporting requirements for stocks and other securities. If passed, the resolution would nullify this reporting requirement before it takes effect.

industries.rationale: The bill directly nullifies a reporting rule imposed on digital asset brokers and DeFi platforms, eliminating a new regulatory compliance obligation.
Traditional financial institutions that offer digital asset services would be relieved of the broker reporting requirements this rule imposed.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the rule titled Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales and issued by the IRS on December 30, 2024.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in your tax bill. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
